headline: 600-Year-Old Peruvian Tomb Opens Its Secrets for the First Time
meta_description: Archaeologists in Peru have unsealed a pristine 600-year-old tomb at Chan Chan containing 38 skeletons and treasures from the elite Chimú civilization.
summary_short: A perfectly preserved tomb at Peru's Chan Chan site has revealed 38 skeletons and priceless artifacts from the Chimú elite—offering the first scientific look at undistur…
body:
Archaeologists in Peru have opened a sealed tomb dating back six centuries, discovering one of the most significant intact burial sites from the Chimú civilization. Located within Utzh An, a palatial complex at the UNESCO World Heritage site of Chan Chan, the tomb contained 38 skeletons along with an extraordinary collection of grave goods: metal weapons, gold and copper artifacts, ornate jewelry, and colorful textiles. For the first time, scientists now have unlooted archaeological data on elite Chimú burials—a breakthrough that anthropologist Gabriel Prieto from the University of Florida called "the discovery of the decade."

What makes this find extraordinary is not just its contents, but what it reveals about how the Chimú honored their dead. At the heart of the tomb, a mausoleum measuring 4 feet wide and 16 feet deep held a single individual whose skull bore traces of red pigment. This person was buried with their body fully extended—an unusual arrangement compared to typical Chimú burials, which were normally flexed or seated. The central chamber branched into two secondary chambers, one holding the remains of 20 people, while 17 other skeletons rested on the platform above.

Previously, everything archaeologists knew about elite Chimú burials came from looted platforms and museum collections—incomplete pictures with no scientific context. This sealed tomb changes that entirely. The Chimú civilization reached its height in the 15th century before the Inca conquered them in the 1460s, yet vast portions of their story remain hidden. Lead excavator Jorge Meneses noted that just 7 percent of Chan Chan has been excavated, suggesting decades of discoveries lie ahead at this remarkable site.
quick_facts: 38 skeletons discovered in a sealed 600-year-old tomb
Located at Chan Chan, a UNESCO World Heritage site in Peru
Contains gold, copper artifacts, weapons, jewelry, and textiles
Only 7% of Chan Chan has been excavated so far
